From a23461c47482fc232ffc9b819539d1f837adf2b1 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Johan Hovold <johan@kernel.org>
Date: Mon, 25 Oct 2021 13:45:30 +0200
Subject: [PATCH] comedi: vmk80xx: fix transfer-buffer overflows

The driver uses endpoint-sized USB transfer buffers but up until
recently had no sanity checks on the sizes.

Commit e1f13c879a7c ("staging: comedi: check validity of wMaxPacketSize
of usb endpoints found") inadvertently fixed NULL-pointer dereferences
when accessing the transfer buffers in case a malicious device has a
zero wMaxPacketSize.

Make sure to allocate buffers large enough to handle also the other
accesses that are done without a size check (e.g. byte 18 in
vmk80xx_cnt_insn_read() for the VMK8061_MODEL) to avoid writing beyond
the buffers, for example, when doing descriptor fuzzing.

The original driver was for a low-speed device with 8-byte buffers.
Support was later added for a device that uses bulk transfers and is
presumably a full-speed device with a maximum 64-byte wMaxPacketSize.

Fixes: 985cafccbf9b ("Staging: Comedi: vmk80xx: Add k8061 support")
Cc: stable@vger.kernel.org      # 2.6.31
Signed-off-by: Johan Hovold <johan@kernel.org>
Reviewed-by: Ian Abbott <abbotti@mev.co.uk>
Link: https://lore.kernel.org/r/20211025114532.4599-4-johan@kernel.org
Signed-off-by: Greg Kroah-Hartman <gregkh@linuxfoundation.org>

diff --git a/drivers/comedi/drivers/vmk80xx.c b/drivers/comedi/drivers/vmk80xx.c
index 9f920819cd74..f2c1572d0cd7 100644
--- a/drivers/comedi/drivers/vmk80xx.c
+++ b/drivers/comedi/drivers/vmk80xx.c
@@ -90,6 +90,8 @@ enum {
 #define IC3_VERSION		BIT(0)
 #define IC6_VERSION		BIT(1)
 
+#define MIN_BUF_SIZE		64
+
 enum vmk80xx_model {
 	VMK8055_MODEL,
 	VMK8061_MODEL
@@ -678,12 +680,12 @@ static int vmk80xx_alloc_usb_buffers(struct comedi_device *dev)
 	struct vmk80xx_private *devpriv = dev->private;
 	size_t size;
 
-	size = usb_endpoint_maxp(devpriv->ep_rx);
+	size = max(usb_endpoint_maxp(devpriv->ep_rx), MIN_BUF_SIZE);
 	devpriv->usb_rx_buf = kzalloc(size, GFP_KERNEL);
 	if (!devpriv->usb_rx_buf)
 		return -ENOMEM;
 
-	size = usb_endpoint_maxp(devpriv->ep_tx);
+	size = max(usb_endpoint_maxp(devpriv->ep_rx), MIN_BUF_SIZE);
 	devpriv->usb_tx_buf = kzalloc(size, GFP_KERNEL);
 	if (!devpriv->usb_tx_buf)
 		return -ENOMEM;
-- 
2.25.1

### Modifications in Each File

1. **File: `drivers/comedi/drivers/vmk80xx.c`**
   - A new macro `MIN_BUF_SIZE` is defined with a value of 64.
   - In the function `vmk80xx_alloc_usb_buffers`, the size of the USB receive buffer (`usb_rx_buf`) is now allocated using the maximum of the endpoint's maximum packet size and `MIN_BUF_SIZE`. This ensures that the buffer size is at least 64 bytes.
   - Similarly, the size of the USB transmit buffer (`usb_tx_buf`) is also allocated using the maximum of the endpoint's maximum packet size and `MIN_BUF_SIZE`.

### Relationships Between Modifications

The modifications in `vmk80xx.c` are directly related to addressing potential buffer overflows that could occur due to insufficient buffer sizes when interacting with USB endpoints. By introducing the `MIN_BUF_SIZE` and ensuring that both the receive and transmit buffers are allocated with a size that is at least 64 bytes, the patch enhances the robustness of the driver against malicious devices that may report a zero or smaller `wMaxPacketSize`. This change is crucial for maintaining data integrity and preventing crashes or undefined behavior in the driver.

Here is the commit message:
comedi: vmk80xx: fix transfer-buffer overflows

The driver uses endpoint-sized USB transfer buffers but up until
recently had no sanity checks on the sizes.

Commit e1f13c879a7c ("staging: comedi: check validity of wMaxPacketSize
of usb endpoints found") inadvertently fixed NULL-pointer dereferences
when accessing the transfer buffers in case a malicious device has a
zero wMaxPacketSize.

Make sure to allocate buffers large enough to handle also the other
accesses that are done without a size check (e.g. byte 18 in
vmk80xx_cnt_insn_read() for the VMK8061_MODEL) to avoid writing beyond
the buffers, for example, when doing descriptor fuzzing.

The original driver was for a low-speed device with 8-byte buffers.
Support was later added for a device that uses bulk transfers and is
presumably a full-speed device with a maximum 64-byte wMaxPacketSize.

Fixes: 985cafccbf9b ("Staging: Comedi: vmk80xx: Add k8061 support")
Cc: stable@vger.kernel.org      # 2.6.31
Signed-off-by: Johan Hovold <johan@kernel.org>
Reviewed-by: Ian Abbott <abbotti@mev.co.uk>
Link: https://lore.kernel.org/r/20211025114532.4599-4-johan@kernel.org
Signed-off-by: Greg Kroah-Hartman <gregkh@linuxfoundation.org>

Here is the root cause:
The bug was caused by the driver using endpoint-sized USB transfer buffers without proper sanity checks on the sizes, which could lead to buffer overflows when accessing the buffers, especially if a malicious device reported a zero or insufficient `wMaxPacketSize`. This oversight could result in writing beyond the allocated memory, leading to potential crashes or undefined behavior.

Here is the patch:
 #define IC6_VERSION		BIT(1)
 
+#define MIN_BUF_SIZE		64
+
 enum vmk80xx_model {
 	VMK8055_MODEL,
 
 static int vmk80xx_alloc_usb_buffers(struct comedi_device *dev)
 {
 	struct vmk80xx_private *devpriv = dev->private;
 	size_t size;
 
-	size = usb_endpoint_maxp(devpriv->ep_rx);
+	size = max(usb_endpoint_maxp(devpriv->ep_rx), MIN_BUF_SIZE);
 	devpriv->usb_rx_buf = kzalloc(size, GFP_KERNEL);
 	if (!devpriv->usb_rx_buf)
 		return -ENOMEM;
 
-	size = usb_endpoint_maxp(devpriv->ep_tx);
+	size = max(usb_endpoint_maxp(devpriv->ep_rx), MIN_BUF_SIZE);
 	devpriv->usb_tx_buf = kzalloc(size, GFP_KERNEL);
 	if (!devpriv->usb_tx_buf)
 		return -ENOMEM;
 
 	return 0;
 }

The code statements that lead to the bug are:
```c
size = usb_endpoint_maxp(devpriv->ep_rx);
size = usb_endpoint_maxp(devpriv->ep_tx);
```
Reason:
The driver was using the `usb_endpoint_maxp` function to determine the size of the USB transfer buffers without any sanity checks. If a malicious device reported a zero or insufficient `wMaxPacketSize`, this could lead to allocating buffers that are too small, resulting in buffer overflows when accessing the buffers.

The code statements that fix the bug are:
```c
size = max(usb_endpoint_maxp(devpriv->ep_rx), MIN_BUF_SIZE);
size = max(usb_endpoint_maxp(devpriv->ep_tx), MIN_BUF_SIZE);
```
Reason:
The patch introduces a minimum buffer size (`MIN_BUF_SIZE`) of 64 bytes, ensuring that the allocated buffers are always at least this size. This prevents buffer overflows by guaranteeing that the buffers can accommodate the necessary data, even if the `wMaxPacketSize` reported by the device is zero or insufficient.
